Gramlot 0.2.5 lets a JavaScript page be one module with `Page` and `Logic`, and adds `gramlot.inout` to send, save and download the data of a page.

## What changes

- A JavaScript page module may export `Page` and `Logic`: `FileHost` takes the module's `Logic` as the page logic. Beside a Python page, `foo.js` is the logic module: its `Logic` is the logic of `foo.py`, and its `Page` export, the JavaScript version of the same page, stays unused. `foo_aux.js` stays admitted; both together are an error. Rules: [GC-090 §030](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/090-classes-and-hosts.md#gc-090-030), [GC-095 §060](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/095-writing-pages.md#gc-095-060).
- The bootstrap HTML carries an import map, with the bootstrap nonce, that resolves `@gramlot/gramlot/page` to the runtime; the runtime exports `Page` and `source`. A page module imported by the browser for its `Logic` loads the runtime already in the page.
- `gramlot.inout`, part of the browser runtime for Python and JavaScript pages: `sendMail` prepares an email with the data as readable lines, `sendHttp` posts them as JSON, `save` and `restore` keep a TYTX file with exact types, `download` exports JSON or XML. Rules: [GC-095 §095](https://github.com/gramlot-org/gramlot/blob/main/docs/public/095-writing-pages.md#gc-095-095).
- The core examples export `Page` and `Logic` from one module; the `_aux.js` companions are gone.

## Upgrading from 0.2.4

- A `foo.js` beside a Python page `foo.py` is now its logic module: it must export `Logic`. A folder that keeps a JavaScript `foo.js` without `Logic` beside `foo.py` adds `export class Logic {}` to it, or moves the JavaScript page to another folder.
- A page with `foo_aux.js` and a module that exports `Logic` (or, for Python, `foo.js` beside it) keeps one of the two.
- A server adapter serves `.css` and `.js` below the pages folder, so the page module and its relative imports reach the browser.
- No other change for pages, in Python or JavaScript.
